title: LLM as judge: model-based evaluation and its limits

videos.script: Some things have no answer key. Is this reply warm? Does it actually answer the question? The tempting fix is to ask another model. {{title}} This lesson builds that judge and then measures it. The judge reads a customer message and two replies, and says which one is better. {{judge}} Sixteen pairs carry a person's verdict. The judge agrees on ten of them. That sounds like most, until you correct for chance. Kappa comes out at a quarter. {{kappa}} Then you swap the order of the replies. The judge changes its mind on six of the sixteen, and each time it picks whichever reply it read first. {{swap}} Three more verdicts survive the swap and are still wrong. In each one the judge chose the longer reply. {{length}} Last, a question about this platform. It grades every exercise you answer, and it never uses a model to do it. You will see exactly why. {{platform}} By the end you know where a judge helps, and where it must never have the last word. {{close}}
